title: algoto — Algorithmic Tool Spec (v1.0)
description: A small annotation layer for algorithmic tools exposed to agents via MCP, CLI or similar. It adds only the meaning the tool's own definition cannot express — names, types and defaults stay where they already live.

^x_.description: Vendor or team extension fields. Anything prefixed x_ is allowed at the top level.

name.description: Must match the tool name or CLI subcommand this document describes.

requires.description: Other tools this one depends on.

algorithm.description: What the tool does under the hood.

description.description: One plain-language line describing the method.
examples: Monte Carlo simulation of the remaining fixtures.

steps.description: Optional short list of the internal steps, in order.

deterministic.description: True if the same inputs always give the same output.

seed_input.description: Name of the parameter that fixes randomness.

approximate.description: True if the output is an approximation rather than an exact answer.

version.description: Version of the underlying algorithm or model.

inputs.description: Extra meaning for input parameters, keyed by parameter name.

outputs.description: Extra meaning for output fields, keyed by field name.

guardrails.description: Constraints across inputs and call limits.

constraints.description: Rules across parameters, stated so agents don't hit them by trial and error.

rule.description: A readable rule over parameter names.

on_violation.description: What happens when the rule is broken.

description.description: What to do instead when the rule is hit.
examples: Lower n_scenarios or shorten the horizon.

rate_limit.description: Call budget in plain words, e.g. 'max 20 calls per minute'.

mode.description: Whether results come back immediately or later.

latency.description: Rough time to run at default inputs.

async.description: Polling hints for paired-tool async patterns.

poll_tool.description: Companion tool to poll for the result.

errors.description: Known failure modes and what to do about them.

examples: The named team is not in the ratings table.
Check the team name against the ratings source first.

role.description: 'data' is what the tool runs on; 'parameter' tunes it; 'seed' pins randomness.

effect.description: How changing this input moves the output.
examples: More scenarios give a smoother estimate but a slower run.

units.description: Units or scale of the field.

uncertainty.description: How uncertainty is expressed for this field.

examples: Probability the team finishes in the top four.
